page.layout: Two printed blocks: the main text column on the left, with a narrow column of marginal notes on the right; a short heading block at the foot of the text; and a note column at the far right margin. Reading order: running head and main column top to bottom, then the heading block, then the notes beside them.

main_text.p: in altitudinem elevata, & divinitus excitata, & ad lumen stellę in modum repræsentandū dispositā, iisdem materia possit esse. Huc referunt etiam Ρ Trajectiones & Stellas cadentes: illa enim est & regio addensati ætheris perpetua: hæ vero non semper ardent, sed splendorem duntaxat trahunt, sicut & in muscis, similibus levibus & viscosis conspicimus. E cum prope terram venerint, extra refractionem videntur extingui, cum duntaxat splendor ob mutatum locum & dispositionem evanescat. Hæc ita Philosophi varie de sublimi meteororū, & non satis explicata materia. Scio alios aliter meteora tractare.
main_text.head: CAPUT DUODECIMUM. ORYCTICA PERIPATETICA, SEU DE METALLIS EX DOCTRINA PERIPATETICORUM.
main_text.p: Oryctica sive de Metallis.Actenus de Meteoria egimus, & Meteora explicavimus: Sequitur corpus Nerterum, quod subtus in terra generatur: diciturq; Fossile, quia è terra effoditur.Corpus ὑεράρον, fossile.

page.notes: Right margin notes: "Oryctica sive de Metallis." and "Corpus ὑεράρον, fossile." The Greek in the first note is badly printed and read as ὑεράρον with doubt. Heading on the printed page reads "ORYCTICA PERIPATETICA" in a decorative capital initial, and the "Ρ" before "Trajectiones" is a Greek word that is only partly legible. The word "Nerterum" is printed so and is left as printed. Show-through from the facing page is ignored.
